open_points.subject: owner-only service API refusal
open_points.text: “opening no listener of the service API, so a service call reaches no Registry and is refused by its connection failing, with no answer”
open_points.question: Does owner-only mode guarantee only that Registry opens no service API listener, or must it also guarantee that every connection to the fixed service API address fails even if another process owns or later acquires that address?
options: Only absence of a Registry listener is guaranteed; another process may accept the connection.
The start must refuse an already-occupied service API address and somehow prevent another process from acquiring it while Registry runs owner-only.
Some deployment control outside Registry must guarantee that the unused address remains unbound.
open_points.default_guess: Guarantee only that Registry opens no service API listener and remove the stronger connection-failure guarantee.

witness.initial: The configuration has no service tokens, all required owner-only checks pass, and another process on VM Platform is listening at the release-fixed service API address.
events: The owner starts Registry in owner-only mode.
Registry skips opening and checking the service API listener as A17 requires.
A service connects to the release-fixed service API address.
outcomes: Following the explicit connection-failure claim, the connection fails and produces no answer.
Following the explicit no-listener implementation, Registry starts successfully but the connection reaches the other process and may receive an answer.
witness.observer: The calling service, and the owner observing whether the connection fails.
